concept: Keyhole b: a heavy lowercase b whose squared bowl is a vault door and whose counter is a keyhole. One closed silhouette with one cutout, drawn on a 4-unit grid inside a 64×64 box.
rationale: The ascender carries the identity. A tall left stem rising above a wide bowl reads as a lowercase b even at 16px, where finer detail is lost. Bitwarden's mark is a symmetric shield split down the middle. This mark is asymmetric, open at the top-left, and has no shield silhouette, point, or vertical split, so the two cannot be confused. The bowl is squared off with large 16-unit radii on the right corners only, so it reads as a solid block or safe door instead of a round letter bowl. That suggests a byte-sized container. The counter is a keyhole (8-unit radius circle plus an 8-unit slot), which makes the 'vault' idea literal without extra parts. Horizontal walls are 8 units and vertical walls 16 units, following type-design contrast so the bowl doesn't look top-heavy. All straight edges sit on multiples of 4, so at 16px every edge lands on a whole pixel: stem 3px, top and bottom walls 2px, keyhole 4px wide with a 2px slot. The same holds at 32, 48, and 128px. The mark is a single filled path with an even-odd cutout, so it inverts cleanly and tints with currentColor.

usage.padding: Inside the 64×64 box the artwork already has 8 units of padding left and right and 4 units top and bottom. At 16px that is 2px and 1px, which suits browser toolbar slots, so use the box as-is for extension icons. Elsewhere, keep clear space equal to the stem width (12/64 of the mark's height) on all sides of the visible artwork. In the lockup, the gap between the bowl's right edge (x=56) and the text (x=72) is 16 units. Keep that ratio when scaling. Text is set at 32 units with baseline y=43, so its ascenders line up with the top of the bowl (y=20) and the text block centres on the mark.
usage.inverted: For dark backgrounds, set the color to #FFFFFF on the SVG or its parent; both SVGs use currentColor. The keyhole is a real cutout, so the background shows through and no extra shapes or knockouts are needed. Never draw a white keyhole on a black mark over a third background color. For an app tile or favicon, use a pure black square (corner radius about 22% of the tile) with the white mark centred at 75% of the tile size. On light backgrounds, use #000000 directly.
usage.color: The mark and wordmark are always pure #000000 or pure #FFFFFF. Neutral grays are for interface surfaces only, for example #F5F5F5 and #E5E5E5 in light themes or #1F1F1F and #2B2B2B in dark themes. Use the black mark on light grays and the white mark on dark grays. Never render the mark itself in gray.
usage.minimum_size: Mark: 16px. Wordmark: 24px tall, which keeps the text at about 12px. Below 24px, use the mark alone.
usage.toolbar_states: Show locked or unlocked state with the extension badge or a popup indicator. Do not show it by graying out or recoloring the mark, so the icon keeps full contrast in the toolbar.
usage.dont: Do not add strokes, outlines, gradients, shadows, or a shield container. Do not rotate the mark or stretch its proportions. Do not change the keyhole's size or position. Do not set 'bytewarden' in a different weight or in all caps.
